correctness.rationale: Exact physiological-time change yields a renewal equation after complete passage through the finite size interval. The unmultiplied characteristic equation is derived by differentiating the boundary response; separate modulus, imaginary-part, and real-axis inequalities settle the full right half-plane. The zero eigenvalue at h′=0 is simple and all nonzero imaginary roots are excluded. A rational cubic factorization gives all positive stationary profiles and derivative signs in the example. Claims deliberately limited to linearized dynamics and no inference of global nonlinear basins.

value.rationale: A finite residence time normally introduces delay-dependent dynamic stability not determined solely by stationary roots. This theorem rigorously identifies a natural constant hazard per size traveled where an exact stationary response slope nevertheless classifies the full infinite-dimensional linear dynamics and rules out oscillatory loss of stability. The nonempty explicit hysteresis interval has two linearly attracting stationary profiles and a linearly unstable middle profile, making it useful as a sharply resolved fixed-flux population benchmark. No downstream nonlinear basin claim or empirical biological claim is required.
